title: Introduction to Information Retrieval
content: Information retrieval is the process of finding relevant information from a collection of documents. Search engines use indexing and ranking methods to return useful results.

title: Boolean Retrieval Model
content: The Boolean retrieval model represents documents using terms and retrieves documents with Boolean operators AND OR and NOT. It is based on exact term matching.

title: Vector Space Model
content: The vector space model represents documents and queries as vectors. TF IDF weights terms and cosine similarity ranks documents by relevance.

title: Inverted Index
content: An inverted index maps each term to the documents that contain it. It makes searching large document collections faster and more efficient.

title: Web Search Engines
content: Web search engines crawl pages, build indexes, process user queries, and rank results. Ranking algorithms consider relevance, quality, and other signals.

title: Natural Language Processing
content: Natural language processing helps computers analyze human language. Tokenization, normalization, stemming, and stop word removal are common text processing steps.

title: Machine Learning
content: Machine learning systems learn patterns from data. Classification, clustering, and neural networks are used in many information retrieval applications.

title: Database Management
content: A database stores structured information and supports efficient querying. Indexes improve lookup speed and database performance.

title: Text Mining
content: Text mining extracts useful patterns and knowledge from unstructured text. It often uses information retrieval, statistics, and machine learning.

title: Evaluation of Retrieval Systems
content: Information retrieval systems are evaluated using precision, recall, F1 score, and ranking measures such as mean average precision.
